result:
In `pricebook.py`, 10 rules didn't match their docstrings. I fixed all 10, using the docstrings as the reference.

**How I checked:** I wrote a separate script that reads the percent, threshold, type (whole/marginal) and cap from each docstring. It builds a reference amount from those using the module docstring's rules. Then it compares that against the real function for quantities 0–259 and 11 different unit prices, across all 150 rules. Before the fixes 10 rules came out different. After the fixes none do.

| Rule | Docstring | What the code did | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 33 (marginal) | cap of 30,000 won on the **discount** | capped the **amount** (qty−20)×unit at 30,000 first, then took 2% of it | take 2% first, then cap the discount |
| 41 | 5+ units | discount only from 6 units (`qty >= 6`) | `qty >= 5` |
| 50 | 12+ units | discount only from 13 units (`qty >= 13`) | `qty >= 12` |
| 63 | cap of 30,000 won | cap applied only when the discount was over 60,000 | cap always applied |
| 113 | cap of 10,000 won on the **discount** | capped the price at 10,000, then took 10% | take 10% of the price, then cap the discount |
| 122 | cap of 50,000 won on the **discount** | capped the price at 50,000, then took 7% | take 7% of the price, then cap the discount |
| 126 | discount rounded down | used `round()`, which rounds to nearest | `// 100` (round down) |
| 136 | 8% | 9% | 8% |
| 143 | whole | computed it like marginal: only (qty−20) units | apply to the whole price `base` |
| 148 | 3% | 4% | 3% |

I left rules 87 and 121 alone. They use `qty > threshold` instead of `>=`, but both are marginal rules. At exactly the threshold quantity the discount is (threshold−threshold)×… = 0, so the result is the same either way.

STATUS: DONE
